L108: L109: L110: L111: L112: L113: L114: L115: Part I L116: L117: Item 1. Business. L118: L119: General L120: The Company is a single-source provider of comprehensive L121: technology-based security solutions for medium and large commercial and L122: government facilities in the United States and abroad. The Company offers a L123: broad range of services, including: (i) consulting and planning; (ii) L124: engineering and design; (iii) systems integration; and (iv) maintenance and L125: technical support. This full range of capabilities enables the Company to L126: provide its clients with any combination of these services or complete turnkey L127: solutions for complex security projects. The solutions provided by the Company L128: include integrated security systems comprised of a command center managing one L129: or more subsystems or components, primarily access control systems, intrusion L130: detection systems, closed circuit television systems, critical condition L131: monitoring systems and fire detection systems. The Company is not aware of any L132: other company whose primary business is to provide this comprehensive range of L133: services on a national basis. L134: The Company serves more than 50 clients including airports, hospitals, L135: prisons, corporations, utilities, universities and government facilities. These L136: clients include Dallas Fort Worth Airport, Nokia, AutoFina, the Hearst L137: Corporation, EDS, Wachovia Bank, MCI WorldCom, Inc. and Alltel Corporation. In L138: addition, in December of 2000 the Company added a Government Division. The L139: Government Division also provides the same full range of security systems L140: services as the Commercial Division. The Company has an open-ended contract with L141: the General Services Administration (GSA) and a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) L142: with the agency that allows the government to purchase materials and services L143: from the Company without having to go through a full competition. The Government L144: Division has completed projects for the U.S. Military and several other L145: government agencies throughout the world. These projects often require L146: state-of-the-art security solutions for classified or high-risk government L147: sites. The clients include the U.S. Army, U.S. Navy, U.S. Airforce, and the L148: Department of Justice. L149: The Company began operations in 1987 in association with a large L150: privately held engineering firm. In 1992, the Company became independent from L151: the engineering firm in conjunction with a capital infusion from a private L152: investment group. Since 1992, the Company has devoted a substantial amount of L153: resources and capital to enhancing its technical capability and services L154: offerings, hiring and training key personnel and expanding its client base. In L155: the fourth quarter of 2000 the Company merged with Security Systems Integration L156: (SSI) through an exchange of stock. This transaction added a very strong L157: Government Division to the Company. In addition to its headquarters office in L158: Springfield, Virginia, which is in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, the L159: Company has regional offices in Atlanta and Dallas and Sacramento, California. L160: Integrated Security Systems L161: Integrated security systems are comprised of one or more subsystems and L162: components that perform a variety of security functions for a facility or group L163: of facilities under the direction of a single command center. The command center L164: consists of a central processor, a common database and software that enable L165: various subsystems and components to communicate with each other and integrate L166: the subsystems and components into a single system. Subsystems and components L167: consist primarily of the following: L168: Access control systems, which are designed to exclude unauthorized L169: personnel from specified areas and provide access control that is typically L170: card-activated. Entry and exit activity can be monitored or recorded and may be L171: controlled on the basis of time and authority level. L172: Intrusion detection systems, which incorporate ultrasonic, infrared, L173: microwave and other sensors to detect unauthorized door and window openings, L174: glass breakage, vibration, motion and noise, and alarms and other peripheral L175: equipment. L176: Closed circuit television systems, which monitor and record entry and L177: exit activity or provide surveillance of designated areas. These systems can L178: deter theft and vandalism and support other access control systems. L608: L609: Overview L610: The Company is a single-source provider of comprehensive, L611: technology-based security solutions for medium and large commercial and L612: government facilities in the United States and abroad. The Company offers a L613: broad range of services, including: (i) consulting and planning; (ii) L614: engineering and design; (iii) systems integration; and (iv) maintenance and L615: technical support. L616: The Company began operations in 1987 in association with a large L617: privately held engineering firm. As a start-up, the Company expended significant L618: capital on the development of the Company's business and infrastructure, and it L619: accumulated losses of approximately $2.8 million from 1987 through 1991 on L620: aggregate revenues of approximately $17.2 million. The Company's revenues from L621: 1990 through 1994 were generated primarily by a contract to design and integrate L622: extensive security upgrades at three nuclear facilities for the Tennessee Valley L623: Authority (the "TVA"). In 1992, the Company became independent from the L624: engineering firm in conjunction with a capital infusion from a private investor L625: group. At the same time, the Company hired new management with extensive L626: expertise in the security industry. Since 1992, the Company has devoted a L627: substantial amount of resources and capital to enhancing its technical L628: capability and services offerings, hiring and training key personnel and L629: expanding its client base. As part of this effort, the Company opened four L630: regional offices in the United States. L631: The Company derives its revenue primarily from long-term, fixed-price L632: contracts. Earnings are recognized based upon the Company's estimates of the L633: cost and percentage of completion of individual contracts. Earned revenue equal L634: the project's total contract amount multiplied by the proportion that direct L635: project costs incurred on a project bear to estimated total project costs. L636: Project costs include direct labor and benefits, direct material, subcontract L637: costs, project related travel and other direct expenses. L638: Clients are invoiced based upon negotiated payment terms for each L639: individual contract. Terms usually include a 25% down payment and the balance as L640: stages of the work are completed. Maintenance contracts are billed either in L641: advance, monthly, or quarterly. As a result, the Company records as an asset, L642: costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings and as a liability, billings L643: in excess of costs and estimated earnings.
